messages:
Sam: Heads-up 1 FinCorp POC kickoff tomorrow. They want BYO-HSM (CloudHSM) with our key-proxy + daily key rotation. Need: perf impact, rotation playbook, attestation flow, and rough POC pricing by EOD today. Who can own?
Priya: I got the questionnaire bits. Quick clarifying q: will FinCorp expect each app request to hit HSM, or are they open to session tokens/cache? that changes both latency and cost.
Jules: They said strict per-request ops for audit reasons. so no session reuse. That will raise tail latency and HSM op counts.
Omar: For strict per-op proxied HSM calls we typically measure median +103ms and p95 +250ms (us-east-1 with CloudHSM). If they insist on multi-region replication, add another ~50ms depending on sync method. These are ballparks; Lena's microbench is more precise.
Aisha: From a security view: they require hardware attestation and proof that Redwood doesn9t expose unwrapped KEKs. We should provide a short Q/A and an attestation acceptance checklist.
Priya: Draft Q/A snippet idea: "Q: Does Redwood persist unencrypted customer keys? A: No. We store only wrapped key blobs; unwrapped key material is never persisted in Redwood systems."
Omar: Also add: "All HSM communications are mutually authenticated (mTLS) and can be restricted to customer network peering/VPC endpoints."
Sam: Pricing thought: POC should include setup/ops one-time fee + per-op surcharge. propose: $2k setup + $0.03 per 1k proxied ops for single-region POC. If they want active-active multi-region HSMs, add $0.01/1k extra and discuss replication costs. Mark as draft.
Jules: Operational note on daily rotation: we can support it, but warn them about the increased number of HSM operations and potential brief error spikes during cutovers. Recommend a rolling canary approach.
Aisha: Can we show them a safety flow for 24h rotation? Something minimal: provision new KEK, publish wrapped variant, 5% canary for 10m, healthcheck, full switch. If they do daily, shorten canary to 5m and monitor.
Sam: Need a small runbook we can include in SOW. Can someone paste a short step list I can copy?
Omar: Paste runbook: "1) Customer provisions new KEK in HSM and provides attestation cert. 2) Redwood ingests wrapped KEK and validates attestation. 3) Route 5% traffic to new KEK for 50m. 4) Monitor errors; if <0.5% fail, continue cutover. 5) Complete rollout; retain previous KEK for decrypt-only per retention window."
Priya: Add note: full rewrap/backfill of stored ciphertext is optional but expensive. recommend keep-old-for-decrypt to avoid bulk re-encrypt costs.
Jules: They asked about outage/failover: if primary HSM region is unreachable, options are: a) customer-managed HSM failover (preferred), b) Redwood-hosted encrypted fallback (needs contract/legal & likely not acceptable for some), c) read-only degrade (allow decrypts only). We need to call out trust tradeoffs.
Sam: FinCorp specifically wants no vendor-managed fallback unless explicitly contracted. So we must include that as an opt-in in the SOW.
Aisha: Attestation exchange details: customer provides HSM vendor cert chain + platform attestation. Redwood validates chain and stores cert fingerprint. For ongoing assurance we can request periodic attestation reports.
Priya: For the security questionnaire, I'll prepare canned answers. Example Q/A: "Q: Can customers use their own HSM? A: Yes. Redwood supports external customer-managed HSMs. Key material never leaves the HSM unwrapped. We perform wrapped operations via mutually authenticated channels. Customer is responsible for HSM provisioning and high-availability setup unless Redwood dedicated fallback is purchased."
Omar: Also include this technical snippet for devs to run a perf check (share with their infra):
```
# quick perf test against key-proxy
time curl -X POST https://keyproxy.redwood.internal/crypto -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"op":"encrypt","key_id":"fin-cek-01","payload":"abc"}'
```
Expect median ~10ms in us-east-1 with VPC peering.
Jules: I'll export our last benchmark CSV and share link. Also adding a short note about connection pooling: even with per-op semantics, TCP/TLS session reuse matters. advise them to enable long-lived connections from app tier.
Sam: Action items: Priya -> canned questionnaire + SOW language; Omar -> perf numbers + runbook; Jules -> latency CSV + test instructions; Aisha -> attestation checklist; Sam -> assemble POC packet and send to FinCorp. Target: EOD.
deploy-bot: Uploaded: fincorp_kms_presales_answers_v1.pdf to /shared/sales/presales/fincorp/
Sam: Thanks team. I'll call FinCorp PM in 30m to align and will flag the no-fallback requirement for legal. :thumbsup:
